title: What is truth, again (John 18:33–38)
hookLine: my kingdom is not of this world

lines: THE ACCUSERS STOP AT THE DOOR.
cards: Early in the morning, John says, the accusers bring Jesus to the governor's palace, then stop at the door. It's the Passover, and they won't go in, so they won't be defiled before the feast.
So Pilate has to keep crossing the threshold: out to the crowd, in to the prisoner, out again. John builds the whole trial that way, scene by scene, outside and inside.
Pilate's well-known question came up early on this path. This time, stay inside the room: a prisoner and a governor alone, and the sentence that started it.

teach.b: Pilate asks: art thou the king of the Jews? For Rome, that's the only question. A king is a rival to Caesar.
Jesus answers, in the Douay-Rheims: "My kingdom is not of this world." It's easy to hear that as: my kingdom is somewhere far away, nothing to do with here.

teach.h: NOT OF: NOT FROM THIS WORLD.
teach.b: But the Greek says ek tou kosmou, out of this world, from it. He's talking about where his kingdom comes from, not where it isn't. It doesn't grow out of armies and taxes and fear.

And he proves it on the spot: if it were that kind of kingdom, his servants would be fighting. A few hours ago, Peter tried, and Jesus told him to put the sword away. Pilate grabs the word: so you are a king?

And Jesus says, "For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth. Every one that is of the truth, heareth my voice." This king doesn't command by force.
His people are the ones who hear his voice: the good shepherd again, sheep who know the voice.

teach.h: NO FLAG GETS THE WHOLE PERSON.
teach.b: Then Pilate asks, what is truth, and walks back out to the crowd without waiting for an answer. Look at the two men.
One keeps crossing a doorway, trying to satisfy the people outside and Caesar far away. The other stands still. A kingdom not from this world isn't a kingdom with nothing to say to this world.
It means a loyalty that no flag, party or boss handed out, so none of them gets the whole person.

how: Catholics hear this exchange every Good Friday, when the Passion according to John is read or sung, often with several voices taking the parts of the narrator, Jesus, Pilate and the crowd.

o: what Jesus was born to testify to
whatever the crowd and Caesar agree on

games.q: you're on trial before a Roman governor, who asks if you're a king. a yes could mean death. what do you say?
o: my kingdom is not of this world.
games.why: Jesus neither denies it nor claims Caesar's kind of power: my kingdom is not of this world. if it were, his servants would fight.

practice: Let the things that pull on you come to mind one at a time: your job, your phone, a team, a party, a person you want to please, your own reputation. Notice honestly which ones get the most of you, without rearranging anything.
If you pray, hold Jesus's words, every one that is of the truth heareth my voice, and listen; if you don't, simply sit with the list.

wordCard.voice: Truth. Pilate's question to a prisoner who had just said his kingdom is not from this world, and who came to testify to the truth. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: truth, the word in Pilate's question (John 18:38).

carryVoice: Your line: not of this world. From somewhere else, with plenty to say here. See you tomorrow.
